title: C3 — the product API envelope
description: interface -> agents. What every product call shares, whatever the instance. The body of each call stays instance-defined and lives in <prefix>-platform/schemas/. The request id travels as the X-Request-Id header and the caller's identity as X-Account-Id / X-Account-Roles; the $defs here describe the same fields as they appear in bodies agents returns. Two call modes: synchronous, and job (start, then poll for per-step progress and the result). Streaming is deliberately absent until a screen needs it.

identity.description: Who is asking, as the interface's backend-for-frontend asserts it. agents trusts it because the backend-for-frontend is the only process that can reach agents (ADR-013); it is never taken from the browser.

response.description: A synchronous call's answer. classification is required: a screen must know what it is showing, and an answer built from classified evidence is that evidence's class.

job_accepted.description: The answer to starting a job. The job keeps the request id of the call that started it; every C6 record a step emits carries it.

job_status.description: Polled until state is succeeded or failed. steps are ordered as the job runs them, so a screen can show each one as it really completes. result is present only on success, error only on failure.

error.description: A typed failure. code is machine-readable; message is for a person and must not carry classified content, because errors reach logs.
